newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Quebec strategy a failure-money managers.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Quebec strategy a failure-money managers.

text.p: The Canadian government's strategy for fighting separatism in the French-speaking province of Quebec is a failure, said a large majority of Canadian money managers in a poll released on Tuesday.
The poll, conducted by the right-leaning Fraser Institute, found that 90 percent of respondents disapproved of the federal government's approach to the "national unity question."
The poll found that 63 percent of respondents thought that Quebec would likely separate within five years. The results mirrored those of a similar Fraser survey released last year.
Quebec voted to remain within Canada by a 50.6 to 49.4 percent margin in a provincial sovereignty referendum in October 1995.

"Canada already pays a price for our 'constitutional malaise' in the form of increased uncertainty and its associated economic costs of high real interest rates and unemployment," said Fazil Mihlar, senior policy analyst with the institute.
"In light of the concerns expressed by the fund managers, Ottawa should redouble its efforts on the unity file in the next parliament," Mihlar said.
Mihlar said that money managers overwhelmingly supported decentralization, which would give all 10 Canadian provinces greater powers, as a way to resolve Canada's constitutional problems.
The poll surveyed 43 money managers responsible for more than C$130 billion in assets. Responses were received between April 15 and May 30, 1997, just before Canada's federal election.
